runs.t: •  Ask and answer What would you do if…?

slides.notes:
Welcome learners as they arrive.
Point to the title and read it: "What Would You Do?" Say: "Imagining situations and making choices: finding money, getting too much change, a free week, a magic wand, a dream job. Learners talk about imaginary situations with If I had / found / were…, I'd…, give reasons, and give advice with If I were you, I'd…. All situations are invented and everyday."
Read the three lines under "Today you will".
Past form, present meaning: If I had a car is about now, not the past. Say it: "I don't have a car. It's imaginary."
Lesson plan: Topic; At a glance: Objectives; Teacher notes.

Step 3 · 6:15–6:30 · Listening + "Hear it, say it" · 15 min (slides 8 to 12). Individuals, then pairs check.
Before you listen (2 min). Say: "This is a radio show called What Would You Do? Mike is the host. He tells a situation, and two people call the show with their answers. Listen: what is the situation?"
There are 3 people: Mike, Grace and Teresa. A narrator starts and ends the listening. Each click highlights the next person.
The audio (L4_L6_listening.mp3, about 1:40) plays the conversation once. Press play again for play 2. A third play is fine if the class needs it.
No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer at a natural, friendly speed, two times. The script says going to and want to. People often say gonna and wanna; learners only need to recognize those words.

slides.notes:
"Hear it, say it" (3 min): Point to the script lines. wanna = want to: "I want to hear your ideas." gonna = going to: "If you're going to call, call early!" Then practice I'd (say the d): I'd give it back, and What would you DO? with the stress on do. The class repeats the two lines twice.
Reductions: the listening says going to and want to. People often say gonna and wanna. Learners only need to recognize the short forms.

slides.notes:
Box 2: possible (If it rains, I'll…) vs. imaginary (If I had a car, I'd…). Each click shows the answer side of one row.
Rule of thumb (read it aloud): Imaginary: use the past form after if (found, had, were). Use would / 'd + base verb in the other half (I'd give, I'd visit). Never put would right after if.

runs.t: advice with If I were you…
If I were you, I'd talk to the supervisor.
If it were one dollar, I'd keep it.
you hear it in speaking; it's OK

slides.notes:
Box 4: If I were you, I'd… for advice. Each click shows the answer side of one row.
Questions and answers (2 min): Q: Can I say If I would have time, I'd take a class? A: No. Never put would right after if: If I had time, I'd take a class. • Q: If I was you or If I were you? A: Write If I were you. In speaking, many people say If I was you. That's OK. • Q: If it rains or If it rained? A: Possible (maybe tomorrow): If it rains, I'll stay home. Imaginary (not real now): If I had a car, I'd drive.
Check questions: "Do I have a magic wand?" (no) "So do I say If I have or If I had?" (If I had) • "If I would have time or If I had time?" (If I had time) • "If I were you or If I am you?" (If I were you).
Lesson plan: Step 4; Grammar Box 4; Questions and answers.

runs.t: Write the correct form of the verb.
Write the correct form of the verb.
If I ____ a wallet, I'd look for the owner. (find)
If I had more time, I'd ____ a computer class. (take)
If I ____ you, I'd tell the truth. (be)
What would you ____ if you won $500? (do)
If she ____ a car, she'd drive to work. (have)
If it rains tomorrow, ____ take the bus. (I'll / I'd)

Step 5 · 7:00–7:15 · Talk Time: What Would You Do? + Magic Wand Chain · 15 min.
Model it first (1 min): read a card: "You find $50 on the floor at work. What would you do?" Help a learner say, "If I found $50, I'd give it to my supervisor because it isn't mine." Say: "Your answer, then because."
Round 1 (7 min): What Would You Do? (groups of 3–4). One person reads a situation card. Each person answers with If I…, I'd… and a reason. The group writes the most common answer. Then the next person reads a card. Each click shows the next step.
15 learners: groups of 3–4 for round 1; then two circles for round 2. 7–8 learners: two groups for round 1; then one circle. 5 or fewer: one group for round 1: you read the cards. Then one circle.

runs.t: ADVICE COLUMN · Ask Gloria: Work and Life
How long are Leo's breaks sometimes?
Where would she talk to him?
Alone, not in front of other people.
When would she talk to the supervisor?
If Leo still took long breaks after that.

slides.notes:
Step 6 · 7:15–7:25 · Read & Write: An advice column · 10 min. Pairs read, then individual writing.
Read (4 min): Learners read a letter to an advice column and the answer on the Read & Write page and answer the questions. Say: "Read fast first. Then find the answers." Pairs answer questions 1–5 together.
Check (1 min): click to show each answer (one click per question, 1 to 5): 1 At a busy restaurant. • 2 30 minutes, not 15. • 3 She'd talk to Leo. • 4 Alone, not in front of other people. • 5 If Leo still took long breaks after that.
Write (5 min): Learners read a short letter about a noisy neighbor and write a reply (5–8 sentences) with If I were you, I'd… because…. Show the example. Invented details are fine. Learners start in class and finish at home (Homework item 2).
If behind: questions 1–5 only; the writing becomes homework.
Lesson plan: Step 6; Read & Write page; Answer key.

runs.t: What would you do if you had a free week?
1. An if-sentence (If I had a free week, I'd…).
Give it to me at the door.
2. Finish your writing from Read & Write C (your reply).

slides.notes:
Step 7 · 7:25–7:30 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP.
Exit ticket (3 min): learners open the Exit Ticket page and answer in 3 sentences with a reason: What would you do if you had a free week? Example on the board: If I had a free week, I'd visit my sister in Chicago. I'd also cook a big dinner for my family. I'd do that because I don't see them very often. With 5 or fewer, a learner can say it to you first and then write it.
Collect the pages. After class, sort them into ✓ / almost / not yet. Start next week with 2 corrections on the board (no names).
Homework (2 min): open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (item 1: if I / have / a free week, I / visit / my cousin → If I had a free week, I'd visit my cousin.). Say: "About 15–20 minutes. Finish your Read & Write writing at home."
Homework items: 1. Write the sentence. Use the words. • 2. Finish your writing from Read & Write C (your reply). Read it one more time. Check ✓ the list in D. • 3. Write 3 sentences about your dreams. Use If I had…, I'd… and a reason. • 4. Review (Lesson 5). Write one word.
Lesson plan: Step 7; Exit Ticket page; Homework page.
